items.title: Daryl Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 11, 2024
items.q: There’s two pianos, she talks, we gab a little bit and then she makes it sound like we’re doing it like just off the cuff

ctx.x: How do you keep a steady gig? I think that’s just basically my question. Or maybe I can turn it around.
By, you know first of all by getting a steady gig like here’s a case in point: The Waldorf. And I remember the day so well. I have to get this in. ’94 I was doing my first show with

Marian McPartland recording at the studio down in the West 30s, and but I was younger then so I wasn’t as crazy and nervous as I am now, so I did that but also just before I left I got a call from an agent who booked The Waldorf asking me if I could go in and play, apparently the piano was in the middle of the lobby at that point. And I said, “Okay, sure, fine.” So after I did her show, and it was the first one where — her format you know of course. There’s two pianos, she talks, we gab a little bit and then she…
